reviews.title: App is better than FITBOD but…
reviews.text:
I really like this app. The AI coaching is useful, and being able to tell it which plates my gym actually has makes the workouts feel tailored instead of generic.
It would be close to perfect with two additions. First, let me specify the bars available, including EZ curl bars and short curl bars, so the suggestions match the equipment I can actually use. Second, keep the workout focused in one area. Right now it sometimes has me leave a bench for a single exercise and then come right back. At a busy gym, holding a bench or a hi-lo is hard, so it would help a lot if the app grouped everything for the muscles I’m working in one spot before moving me to the next station.
That small change would make the sessions much easier to follow in a real gym.

reviews.title: The App Is OK-ish
reviews.text:
Just like the title says. I can see where people would find this app useful. It has promise, but I think the developers rushed the launching. 

The “AI” is nothing really to write home about. I asked it how I could do a completed workout again and it gave me two different answers. 

The lack of Landmine exercises. 

The lack of Kettlebell exercises. 

The feature that allows you to suggest an exercise isn’t all that great because the “post” button is continually grayed out. 

The support from an actual human is atrocious. If you ask the staff a question, they’ll mark the ticket as closed without any explanation or resolution. 

All-in-all, be cautious about using this app. Don’t expect great things and take it for what it’s worth.

reviews.title: Great App! One Suggestion
reviews.text:
Incredible app, basically a personal trainer in your pocket
I think this app is fantastic and hands down the only workout app I use.

What makes it great:
* For beginners: It takes away all the guesswork if you don’t know where to start or how to structure a routine.

* For experienced lifters: It eliminates decision fatigue. Having the app program your sessions feels just like working with a personal trainer.

* Smart progression: The adaptive weight suggestions (and set tracking) feel incredibly spot on, almost like it reads your notes and adjusts intensity automatically.

Room for improvement / Feature request:
I’d love to see more cardio features integrated down the road like tracking running workouts or custom cardio sessions besides is already there. It’s primarily a strength app and does that exceptionally well, but expanded cardio would make it a complete all-in-one platform.

Bug report for developers:
The only minor issue occurs when using the search tool to swap or replace an exercise. The search occasionally glitches, images overlap, or the app freezes momentarily.

Overall, I wish I’d found this app years ago and can't wait to see how it evolves. Keep up the awesome work!

reviews.title: Best app on the market
reviews.text:
This app is incredible. I moved to it about a month ago after years on FitBod and am blown away. I was hesitant to move over because I thought “how different can it be”. 

The workouts are more logical based on my 15 years of lifting experience. On FitBod I was editing the workout all the time to make it more sense (ex it would recommend 2-3 different types of deadlifts on the same day) 

The workouts have also pushed me harder than I’ve worked out in a long time. I didn’t realize how much I was leaving on the table every lift. I’m feeling stronger, bigger and better than I have in a long time. 

The Garmin App is a game changer. Keeps me from having to pull out my phone all the time and getting distracted by something else on my phone. 

Can’t wait to see how it progresses over the next few months.
